title: The task page question card reads rulings without the live-run guard
description:
Follow-up from LIN-4114 research. The feed (`routes/dashboard-rulings.js:99`) and the session page (`routes/dashboard-session-state.js:243`) pass `liveDispatchOnAnchor`, so an answer on a task with a live run only records. The task page's ruling read (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1236`, `:1385` via `readRulingStanding`) passes none, so its card can start a run that collides with one in flight. LIN-4114 adds an optional live-guard parameter to `readRulingStanding` for Home only and leaves the task page unchanged on purpose (it would change this surface's behaviour).

Done when: the task page's card has the same effect as the feed's for the same loops.

Witness: a task with a live run and an open ruling; the task page's card row has `effect: 'record'`, as the feed's row does.

## How to go about it

*Survey findings pruned at close-out (full text in the task snapshots). Outcome: the reported task-page card was already guarded; the real collision path was the client defaulting a missing* `data-effect` *to* `resume`*; the scope decision below was followed.*

### Scope decision (5 Nov, about 05:10 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and to err on the side of larger tidies. **The decision: settle the premise with a test, then close the real collision path and leave one way to read standing.** In pieces:

1. **The witness first, run at the base.** A loader-plus-render test: a task with a live run and an open ruling; assert the card's `data-effect`. If it passes before any change (expected), say so plainly on the ticket: the reported card is already guarded, and why.
2. **Fail closed in the client.** An empty or missing `data-effect` means `record`, not `resume`, so no surface can start a run from a row whose effect wasn't decided. A red test: a card with no effect, pressed while a run is live, starts no run.
3. **One way to read ruling standing.** Make the live guard unconditional in `rulingStandingOf` (remove the `liveGuard` parameter), so the task page's reads and `buildRowStates`' fallback are guarded too. Update LIN-4242's foil to compare against the raw collection, and the three comments above. If this changes anything a user sees on the task page, stop and say what.

**At merge (we'll check it):**

* no reader of ruling standing can skip the guard (no parameter to forget);
* a card with an undecided effect cannot start a run;
* the comments that list the guard's consumers describe the code as it is.

**Not this task's:** `routes/proxy-rulings.js:247`'s own copy of the live predicate (instead of `liveOnAnchor`); the re-export shim in `routes/dashboard-session-state.js`; the 30-day vs all-time liveness scope difference.

## Implementation Plan

**Session fit:** fits one session
**plan-review due: no** (it tightens a guard rather than loosening one, touches no credentials, merge rules or dispatch contract, and is one focused session)

### Implemented

Implemented as approved, in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2285](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2285>) (merged as 2eb73ae07fb7297fc0fa057a6198aa8cbe901558): witness test, fail-closed card default (`public/question-cards.js`), characterization test, and the unconditional live guard in `rulingStandingOf` (the `liveGuard` parameter and `liveDispatchOnAnchor` override removed). No deviations from the plan. The full plan, findings and decisions are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
LIN-4143 — PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2285 (head 568bc8b9, branch feat/lin-4143-task-page-live-guard). CI green on the head: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan, and CI success all SUCCESS.

What landed, in four commits:
1. Witness (green at base): the task page card has the feed's effect for the same loops. The card was already guarded: its rows come from the run page's guarded read. The ticket's literal `record` holds for a waiting ruling with message text and no wake marker; a `[blocked]` ruling with a live run reads `resume` on both paths.
2. The question card fails closed: an absent or empty `data-effect` now means `record`, not `resume`. This was the real collision path. Red first, then green.
3. Characterization (green at base) pins the standing shape: live run, task-scan decision, shelves, parked loop.
4. The `liveGuard` flag and the `liveDispatchOnAnchor` override are removed from `rulingStandingOf`. The guard is unconditional. Call sites, comments, the LIN-4242 foil and the LIN-4114 feed comparison are updated.

Evidence that the task page is unchanged: its rendered HTML, header, status and waiting state are byte-identical before and after across 18 scenarios. The standing effect does change for the no-marker wait (null to record), so the comparison is not vacuous. The LIN-4114 GUARD test changed from dispatch to record by design, since it pinned the unguarded read this ticket removes.

Behaviour to know: a resumable card with an absent data-effect now records instead of resuming. No current renderer omits the attribute on a resumable card.

## Review — LIN-4143

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2285, head `568bc8b993207985a0994e5c7f12cf5f7f4e065a` (4 commits on base `c70b004c`).

CI: green on head 568bc8b9 — Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan (source), CI success all SUCCESS.

### Scope vs plan
The diff is the plan's own list: `lib/ruling-standing.js`, `lib/unanswered-decisions.js` (`rulingStandingOf`, `resolveEffect` doc), `lib/home-row-states.js`, `lib/live-anchor.js` header, `lib/task-page-loader.js` (a comment only; its three call sites become guarded with no edit), `public/question-cards.js:369`, and the tests named in the plan. Nothing outside the plan was touched. `proxy-rulings.js`, the `dashboard-session-state.js` shim and the liveness scope are all unchanged, as required. All three "at merge" checks hold:
- **No reader can skip the guard.** `grep liveGuard lib routes public` finds nothing. `rulingStandingOf` now takes only `{ now, enrichLoop }` and always passes `liveOnAnchor(tagged)`. The `liveDispatchOnAnchor` override is gone, and it had no callers.
- **An undecided effect cannot start a run.** The card default is now `'record'`. Every card goes through `renderQuestionCard`, which always emits `data-effect`. The bare-blocked card hard-codes `effect: 'resume'` with `disposition: 'resumable'`, so no legitimate resume loses its effect.
- **The comments match the code.** The `live-anchor.js` consumer list, the `ruling-standing.js` doc, the `rulingStandingOf` doc (the "off by default" text is removed) and the `resolveEffect` branch-4 note all describe the code as it is.

### Regression check
`git log -6` on each touched file: the most recent changes are LIN-4242/4241/4114/4173/4040. None of them fixed something this PR undoes. LIN-4114's `liveGuard: true` for Home is subsumed: Home's call is unchanged in behaviour, since it is still guarded. The `|| 'resume'` default came from LIN-3252 (`607d0c18`) and was moved by LIN-3499 (`c08f56a0`), with no recorded reason for defaulting to resume. Staleness: files changed since the ticket was created (LIN-4243/4242/4241) were re-read at HEAD. The plan's findings hold there, and the description's "unguarded card" premise is stale, as the plan says.

### Mutation checks (LIN-2274). Each mutation went red, then was reverted; tree clean.
1. `public/question-cards.js:369` default set back to `'resume'` → 4 `session-question-card-effect` fail-closed tests fail (absent and empty effect × indeterminate and gone).
2. `rulingStandingOf` loses its predicate (`{ now }` only) → 5 fail: the LIN-4114 Home witness and differential, LIN-4114 GUARD, the LIN-4143 characterization "no guard argument reads LIN-5 as record", and LIN-4242 witness 3.
3. `deriveSessionDecisions` (`routes/dashboard-session-state.js:243`) loses its predicate → the LIN-4143 task-page witness ("the card reads record, as the feed does") fails. The witness really pins the card's guard source.
Touched suites, run locally (lin-4143/4114/4242, session-question-card-effect, reply-delivery-contract, task-page-question, question-card-task-bound): 197/197 pass.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "a ruling row's effect read without the live predicate, or defaulted when undecided." I checked these siblings:
- Direct `collectUnansweredDecisions` callers without a predicate: `lib/chat-tools.js:1758`, `lib/ticket-close-closer.js:98,114`, `routes/dashboard-kpis.js:70`. None reads or emits `effect`, so none can drive an answer. They are not instances of the defect; no action.
- Client: `deliverRulingAnswer` is called only from `public/question-cards.js`. The Rulings tab (`public/observation.js`) answers from feed rows, which are always guarded. The helper's absent→`resume` contract (`reply-delivery-contract.test.js`) is left alone by design and is now reachable only through markup, which fails closed.
- `routes/proxy-rulings.js:247`'s inline predicate: **outside**, explicitly excluded by the scope decision (it is guarded, just duplicated).
With those checked, the change covers the class.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (scope decision step 3, "if this changes anything a user sees on the task page, stop"): the claim that the task page shows no visible change rests partly on the builder's 18-scenario byte-identical HTML probe, which is not committed. The committed characterization test pins rows, `openLoopIds`, `shelvedTaskIdentifiers` and `taskScanByIdentifier` agreeing with the raw reduction, but not rendered HTML. Grep found nothing under `lib/task-*.js` / `lib/home-*.js` that reads `.effect` from standing, which supports the claim. **Before the merge:** close-out re-runs `grep -n "\.effect" lib/task-*.js lib/home-*.js routes/dashboard-task*.js` at the merge commit. Wrong means any hit that reads a standing row's effect into the task page's output.
- **Inside** (fail-closed card, scope decision step 2): the fail-closed path is driven only in the vm harness with the real `common.js`; no e2e presses a card with no effect in a real browser. A browser cannot behave differently on `dataset.effect || 'record'`, and E2E is green across all card surfaces, so the harness covers it. **Before the merge:** no further check needed beyond confirming `ci-success` is green on the merge commit.
- **Inside** (plan risk 3, cost): the builder did not report timing for `gatheredStateOf` on a large subtree. I settled it by reading the code: `liveOnAnchor` is a closure, and the `.some` scan runs only for rows that reach `resolveEffect` branch 4 (non-resumable), over one subtree's 30-day windowed loops. That is less than the feed already does per workspace. Discharged by inspection; no measurement taken.
- **Inside**, after the deploy (optional live check): on a production task with an open ruling (waiting with no wake marker, or task-bound) and a second live run on the same anchor, the task page card's `data-effect` is `record`, and pressing it starts no new dispatch. It is not a merge condition. Rollback: revert the squash-merge commit of #2285 (no migration and no persisted data shape, so it is fully reversible).

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The PR meets all three merge checks. Each load-bearing test went red under the mutation of its own code path, and CI is green on head 568bc8b9. What remains is a grep re-check at merge and an optional post-deploy live check.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** The code change was not hard: a one-line client default and the removal of one parameter. The difficulty was that the ticket described a bug that did not exist. The card was already guarded, so the effort went into proving negatives: that the card already matched the feed, and that removing the flag changed nothing a user sees. Two awkward spots:
- The characterization was meant to stay green before and after, but its comparator (`liveGuard: true`) was the thing being removed. I rewrote part of it in the change commit, which weakens "written first".
- The LIN-4114 `GUARD` test deliberately pinned the old unguarded read, so it had to flip.

**2. What I'd have done first.** The probe: build the task page model across loop shapes and compare it with the feed's reduction and the raw one. It told me more than the ticket did. I'd also run the before/after HTML differential first, not last, because it settles "stop if anything user-visible changes" in one step.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- The bare-blocked card hard-codes `resumable`/`resume` whatever the loop's real state.
- The LIN-4242 scenario key `liveGuard` names a flag that no longer exists.
- The new test files are named after the ticket, not after what they pin.

**4. The ticket I'd have wanted.** "The question card fails closed when its effect is undecided": one commit, one red test. Separately: "ruling standing has one call shape".

**5. What the ticket and plan got wrong.**
- The premise: the card was not unguarded.
- The literal witness: a `[blocked]` ruling with a live run reads `resume` on both surfaces, not `record`.
- The plan said `record` shows on the task page for a waiting loop with no marker. That holds only if the loop has message text. Without it, no producer is named and `buildQuestion` drops the row, a row-presence rule nobody had mentioned.

**6. What the change left behind.**
- Two defaults now disagree: the card treats an absent effect as `record`, `ReplyDelivery` as `resume`. The mismatch is pinned, but any new caller of `deliverRulingAnswer` without an effect inherits the fail-open default.
- The live predicate is built in three places (feed route, `deriveSessionDecisions`, `rulingStandingOf`), and `proxy-rulings` keeps its own inline copy.
- The 30-day vs all-time liveness scope gap is untouched.
- Simpler: no flag, one standing call shape, and a header comment that lists the real consumers.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** Mildly, yes.
- The fail-closed card was the only real fix, and it lived in the larger scope. A minimal "add the guard to the task page" ticket would have found nothing to change.
- Removing the flag caused churn across four test files. It bought "no reader can forget the guard", and the differential showed it cost nothing visible.
- The witness commit tests something that was never broken. It earns its place as a record, not a fix.
- I'd have drawn the line where it ended, but would fold the `ReplyDelivery` default into the same decision instead of leaving a mismatch.

## Close-out — LIN-4143

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2285, squash-merged as `2eb73ae07fb7297fc0fa057a6198aa8cbe901558`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 568bc8b993207985a0994e5c7f12cf5f7f4e065a`. Review verdict was Approve, conditional on this close-out discharging the ledger.

**Changes I made after approval:** none. Review asked for no code fixes, only a grep re-check and an optional post-deploy check. The merged tree is exactly the reviewed head, and base `main` had not moved (`c70b004c`).

**CI:** CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Fresh read before merge: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan (source) and CI success were all SUCCESS on head 568bc8b9, with merge state CLEAN. Because base had not moved, the merge commit's tree is the CI-tested tree.

### Ledger
1. **Inside, pre-merge: the "task page shows no visible change" claim.** Review's condition was to re-run `grep -n "\.effect" lib/task-*.js lib/home-*.js routes/dashboard-task*.js`. I re-ran it at the PR head (no `routes/dashboard-task*.js` file exists, so I used `routes/*task*`): **0 hits**. Nothing under those paths reads a standing row's effect into the task page's output. `grep -rn liveGuard lib routes public` also returns 0 hits. Settled.
2. **Inside, pre-merge: fail-closed card in a real browser.** Review required only `ci-success` green. It was SUCCESS. Settled.
3. **Inside: cost of `gatheredStateOf`.** Review discharged it by inspection. Nothing further was asked.
4. **Inside, post-deploy: the card on a production task.**
   - *Deploy landed:* the harbour.cat footer moved from `c70b004c` to `2eb73ae0…` (the merge) at about 06:10 UTC.
   - *Verified on what landed:* the served `question-cards.js` line 369 reads `var effect = card.dataset.effect || 'record';`.
   - *Not run:* the full live check (a production task with an open ruling and a second live run on the same anchor; `data-effect` is `record`; pressing starts no dispatch). I have no way to create that state on production without starting real dispatches. Who can run it: an operator with a production task in that state. It did not hold the close.
5. **Named rollback:** revert the squash-merge commit `2eb73ae0` (no migration, no persisted data shape). There is no named monitor, and I am not supplying one.
6. **Outside:** `routes/proxy-rulings.js:247`'s own copy of the live predicate. Existing ticket **LIN-3843** already names that file and finding, so I linked it as `related` and filed nothing new. The `dashboard-session-state.js` re-export shim and the 30-day vs all-time liveness scope were explicitly excluded by the scope decision and are unchanged.

**Notes for the record:** the ticket's original premise (the task page card is unguarded) was stale. The card was already guarded, and the real collision path was the client defaulting a missing `data-effect` to `resume`. The ticket's literal witness text (`effect: 'record'`) holds only for a waiting ruling with no wake marker. A `[blocked]` ruling with a live run reads `resume` on both paths.

**Final CI state:** green on 568bc8b9. Merged as 2eb73ae0. Deployed and serving 2eb73ae0.

relatedIssue.title: Rulings live-on-anchor predicate is duplicated in routes/proxy-rulings.js and routes/dashboard-session-state.js, and one comment points at moved code
